interface: Game.exe VM wrapper and image-wrapper helpers; not native PAL DLL exports
behavior: Legacy parent/child accepted slot range is -1..128 inclusive; newer is -1..127 inclusive. Parent or positive child absent is success1 without mutation.
Child -1 clears entire parent lane flag and child slot. Other negative child values fail range check.
Positive child stores high attachment bit0x10000000 on the parent lane, but transform auxiliary storage belongs to the child wrapper; multiple parent lanes share that child bank.

Store scale delta parent_base*child_base-parent_base, independently for X/Y in newer. Store child-parent rotation difference. Store each child base ARGB byte minus255 as signed16. X/Y offsets store native32bit integers.
Per tick: parent slots0..63 then child lanes0..7; copies summed parent color/scale/position/rotation to child base. Child keeps its auxiliary bank, so its deltas are added on final PAL submission.

Center adjustment uses half of PalSpriteGetWidth/Height (cell dimensions), integer center differences and truncation of center_difference*parent_scale before wrapped subtraction. It does not add native sprite image offsets.
Parent Z replaces child base Z before child auxiliary Z contributions; previous output is not accumulated.
Native malformed child_lane is not bounded and writes invalid memory; the portable adapter rejects values outside0..7.
portable_state: Shared child offsets and ordered parent/lane references persist in portable version13 tail.
remaining_boundaries: Full native image-wrapper auxiliary animation banks remain separate from portable SpriteActionLanes.
Repeated reattachment after independently changing wrapper base fields needs a complete wrapper base-state representation; attachment captures the current portable base properties.
The native float-angle mode flag and every integer-angle quantization stage are not separately modeled by this adapter.
review_basis: Native setter disassembly and exact stack pops
All three walk order and parent bounds
Native scalar and SIMD transform consumers
PAL integer/float rotation exports separately declared in reverse/abi/graphics32.json
